title: Takayama vs Kanazawa: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Kanazawa for packed sightseeing and short stays; Takayama for rural Japan atmosphere, Hida beef, and onsen. Do both if you have 4+ days.

categories.name: Historic Districts
categories.summary: Sanmachi Suji is Japan's best-preserved Edo merchant district. Kanazawa's chaya districts are smaller but Kenroku-en is world-class.

categories.name: Food & Dining
categories.summary: Takayama wins for Hida beef and sake breweries; Kanazawa wins for seafood and Omicho Market.

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: Kanazawa is slightly cheaper to reach and has more budget accommodation options.

categories.name: Access
categories.summary: Kanazawa is 2.5h from Tokyo by Shinkansen; Takayama requires 4.5h via Nagoya.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Kamikochi, Shirakawa-go, and Oku-Hida onsen are all accessible from Takayama.

categories.name: Onsen
categories.summary: Oku-Hida onsen village is spectacular; Kanazawa has limited in-city options.

categories.name: City Size
categories.summary: Kanazawa (458k pop) has more restaurant and cultural options than Takayama (88k).

faq.question: Is Takayama or Kanazawa better for first-timers?
faq.answer: Kanazawa for 1-2 nights; Takayama when you want to slow down and have 2+ nights.

faq.question: Can I visit both?
faq.answer: Yes — Nohi Bus via Shirakawa-go connects them in 2h 45min.
